record.provider: Epic Online Services Player Data Storage

free_tier.stated: 400 MB total storage per user, 200 MB maximum per file, 1,000 files per user. No published product-level or title-level byte cap.

egress.terms: No per-GB egress meter documented for Player Data Storage; access is metered as API requests. EOS itself is free for all developers.

record.tooling: EOS SDK (C/C++), C# and Unreal plugins (PlayEveryWare/eos_plugin_for_unity). File ops are chunked read/write callbacks: EOS_PlayerDataStorage_WriteFile / ReadFile / QueryFileList. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: 400 MB per ProductUserId x unlimited free player identities. EOS supports anonymous/device auth, so identities are mintable at will; each new ProductUserId is a fresh 400 MB bucket. 2,500 identities = 1 TB.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 200 MB per file and 64-character filename limit; request-rate: ~1,000 read or write requests per minute per user, then EOS_PlayerDataStorage_UserThrottled; per-object-cap: 1,000 files per user. Retention: none stated. Files persist until explicitly deleted; no expiry found. Data is encrypted at rest with a client-side key EOS never stores, so losing the key loses the bytes.
record.reliability_note: Throttles writes (not errors) once the 400 MB per-user total is reached until files are deleted; quota is per-deployment so a busy title can hit service-level allocation failures.

evidence.proved: filename format, 64-char limit, encryption-key requirement, 'Data that you store through this interface is accessible to players (users) on any device'

quotas table 'Maximum individual file size 200 MB / Total storage space per user 400 MB / Maximum files per user 1000' (secondary source, corroborates the SDK error codes EOS_Result_PlayerDataStorageFileSizeTooLarge and _UserThrottled)
'Each service applies usage quotas on a per-deployment basis'
